n=len(t)
seq=['A']*n
pairs={}
stack=[]
for i,c in enumerate(t):
    if c=='(': stack.append(i)
    elif c==')':
        j=stack.pop(); pairs[j]=i; pairs[i]=j
# design: assign complementary pairs
# outer helix positions
design={
 # H1 5-8 <-> 107-110
 (5,'G'),(6,'G'),(7,'C'),(8,'C'),(107,'G'),(108,'G'),(109,'C'),(110,'C'),
 # wait complement: 5 pairs 110, 6 pairs 109, 7 pairs 108, 8 pairs 107
}
# Let me do programmatically: define per-helix sequences (5'->3' on the left side), right side is reverse complement
helix_defs=[
 (5,8,107,110,'GGCC'),   # left seq 5->8, right 107->110 is revcomp reversed
 (10,13,31,34,'GCGC'),
 (19,22,26,29,'GCUA'),
 (38,40,80,82,'GCG'),
 (43,45,58,60,'GCG'),
 (46,48,52,54,'CUC'),
 (61,63,76,78,'GCG'),
 (64,66,70,72,'CUC'),
 (86,88,103,105,'GCG'),
 (92,94,99,101,'CUC'),
]
comp={'A':'U','U':'A','G':'C','C':'G'}
for l_start,l_end,r_start,r_end,lseq in helix_defs:
    # left side positions l_start..l_end get lseq
    for k,ch in enumerate(lseq):
        seq[l_start+k]=ch
    # right side: position r_start pairs with l_end, r_start+1 with l_end-1...
    # so right side sequence (5'->3' from r_start to r_end) is revcomp of lseq
    rc=''.join(comp[c] for c in reversed(lseq))
    for k,ch in enumerate(rc):
        seq[r_start+k]=ch
print(''.join(seq))
print('len',len(seq))
"
